correctness.rationale: The five maximal independent supports of C5 are the five diagonals, so the corresponding joins cover the complex and form a transitive family. On a chosen pair, any group identification between two points of two-position support belongs to the pair stabilizer. On singleton support, it is either equality or the stabilizer swap since inner labels cannot change. Thus the map from the swap quotient of one join onto the full geometric orbit space is bijective as well as continuous, and compact–Hausdorff makes it a homeomorphism. This uses points with nonzero barycentric mass, including points on inverted faces, not only face or vertex orbits. For (d+1)K2 the fibre is the crosspolytope-boundary sphere; the sphere-join model is equivariant by using coordinates (sqrt(1-t)x,sqrt(t)y). Diagonal and antidiagonal coordinates conjugate the swap to a sign on the second sphere factor, and the resulting orbits are exactly the join with RP^d, including endpoints. The unreduced iterated suspension is homotopy equivalent to the based version for this based connected CW complex. The alternating 0,2 cellular differential of RP^d gives the stated integral groups after d+1 suspensions; in d=2 the degree-two attaching map suspends to the cofiber S^4 ∪_2 e^5, giving the Moore-space type, not just the same homology. For the unquotiented comparison one can also use the short exact cellular chain sequence from the five pairwise overlaps, the five joins and their union (each fibre occurs in exactly two joins, with no triple overlaps); the overlap-to-joins map induces zero in positive degrees for these sphere fibres, and its degree-zero map is the pentagon incidence matrix. This gives free reduced homology in degrees 1,d+1,2d+1. Independent /workspace/evidence/pentagon.py (pentagon.txt) recovers the bounded face-orbit counts by Burnside using the number of fibre faces, not by running the packaged script. Face counts alone do not establish a geometric quotient theorem.

value.rationale: There is a useful geometric quotient identification for arbitrary fibre, not just a torsion number. It gives an infinite and explicit family where ordinary dihedral quotients acquire integral 2-torsion although the original complex has free homology. The support-overlap argument also explains why naive vertex identification or nonfree rational transfer cannot by itself recover the integral orbit topology.
